proposed.text: If the identity of a wood species is not known and working stresses cannot be found in Table 615.2-1, what does NSCP Section 622.1 allow?

options.text: Machine-graded lumber can be used for general and structural applications.
Any unmarked hardwood may be treated as High Strength Group timber.
Fiberboard or hardboard may automatically replace structural timber.
All design values must be taken from the Yakal row.

rationale.correct: Section 622.1 permits machine-graded lumber when species identification is unknown and working stresses cannot be found in Table 615.2-1.
rationale.b: Not selected: The checked source does not allow unknown species to be treated as High Strength Group timber.
rationale.c: Not selected: The checked anchors do not support fiberboard or hardboard substitution claims.
rationale.d: Not selected: The Yakal row cannot be applied to unknown species.
rationale.takeaway: Unknown-species timber questions move to the Section 622 machine-graded lumber path.
rationale.source_boundary: Batch 162 uses only NSCP OCR page-0889.md lines 5-65 and page-0943.md lines 51-96.

proposed.explanation: Section 622.1 is the source-supported path when species identity is unknown and Table 615.2-1 cannot provide working stresses.
